description: Golden corpus for the analytics epic (#310), one file per scenario listed in #308.
Six-handed $1/$2 NLHE, every stack $200 (100bb), rake free, so each amount is exact
and a wrong pot is a wrong number rather than a rounding question.
The button is always seat 3, so each seat keeps one role across the whole corpus:
seat 1 Anna is the hijack (position 2), seat 2 Boris the cutoff (1), seat 3 Cara the
button (0), seat 4 Dave the small blind (S), seat 5 Erin the big blind (B), seat 6
Frank under the gun (3). Boris is the recorded hero in every hand.
Expectations use the semantic vocabulary in tests/helpers/analytics_golden.py.

note: street0OpenLimp is set for the first preflop caller, whether or not the pot was
raised, so a player who calls an open is recorded exactly like a player who limps
an unraised pot. Poker says an open-limp is entering an unraised pot; only two rows
in this corpus (Frank in hands 3100000002 and 3100000031) are real open-limps, the
other 27 are calls
of a raise. The corpus pins the count so a fix to the rule is visible here instead
of silently changing every limp-based stat.
calcFlopStats returns as soon as it fails to find a preflop aggressor, so a pot
nobody raised loses every flop flag it would otherwise set: the fold of the big
blind in hand 3100000031 is a flop fold the row does not carry, although enum_folded
records the street correctly. Twenty players fold a flop in this corpus and nineteen
rows say so. The count is pinned so that lifting the guard shows up here.
street0Limp is documented as the over-limp flag but calcLimpStreet0 leaves it False
for an over-limp as well as for an open-limp, so an over-limper is indistinguishable
from a player who never entered the pot. Hand 3100000002 has Anna over-limp behind
Frank, which is why that hand is the one asserting it.
One of the 30 rows that carry raisedFirstIn is an iso-raise over limpers, and the
same row has raiseFirstInChance false: the pipeline both denies the opportunity and
records the deed. Poker (and PT4) exclude pots opened by limpers from RFI, so RFI
stats over-count limped pots, and a stat computed as raisedFirstIn over
raiseFirstInChance can exceed 100 percent. Hand 3100000002 pins it.
One of the 22 rows that carry street1CBDone is a preflop aggressor who checked the
flop, faced a donk bet and check-raised (hand 3100000010, Boris). Poker counts that
as a check-raise, not a continuation bet, and the pipeline records the check-raise
correctly in street1CheckRaiseDone -- so a c-bet-frequency stat built on
street1CBDone over-counts check-raises.
foldToOtherRaisedStreetN reads "folded to a raise on street N", but the aggression
pass that feeds it counts a bet as a raise, so folding to an ordinary lead sets it
too: in hand 3100000003 Anna bets the turn, nobody raises, and Boris's fold is
recorded as a fold to a turn raise. Anything built on the column therefore reads
fold-to-bet and fold-to-raise as one number. The turn count is pinned so that
separating the two shows up here.
effStack is min(own remaining stack, largest opponent remaining stack) taken from the
stacks as the parser left them once the betting is in, not from the stacks at the
start of the hand. With everyone on 100bb it reports 19800 for a big blind and 19900
for a small blind instead of 20000, and a player who is all-in for their whole stack
reports that whole stack. Hand level stack buckets built on this are shifted by the
money already committed.
One of the 19 rows that carry foldToStreet1CBDone is a player who bet the flop and
folded to a raise (hand 3100000010, Cara). The flop aggressor raised rather than
continuation bet, so the poker-correct flag is fold-to-a-raise, which the pipeline
records separately in foldToOtherRaisedStreet1.

logic: Everyone folds to the cutoff, who opens to 2.5bb and takes the blinds down.
The reference case for an unopened pot: one voluntary entrant, one raise, no flop.
Because the raise comes from the cutoff with everyone folded, it is also a steal.

Boris.role: cutoff open-raising 2.5bb and winning preflop

Dave.role: small blind folding to the steal

Erin.role: big blind folding to the steal, its blind already out of its stack

logic: Frank open-limps, Anna over-limps behind him, and the cutoff iso-raises to 5.5bb
over both limpers; everyone folds and the limpers do not contest it.
Two things worth pinning: an open-limp and an over-limp are not the same event, and
the iso-raise is not an unopened-pot raise even though it is the first raise.

Boris.role: cutoff iso-raising over two limpers

Frank.role: under the gun open-limping, then folding to the iso-raise

logic: The hijack opens and the cutoff calls, so the opener plays the flop out of position.
Both check the flop; the opener then bets the turn, which is a delayed c-bet rather
than a c-bet, and the caller folds.
This is the corpus reference for who is in position after an open-call.

Anna.role: hijack opener, out of position throughout

Boris.role: cutoff calling the open, in position on every street

logic: The hijack opens, the cutoff 3-bets to 8bb, the opener calls, and the 3-bettor
c-bets the flop in position and takes it down.
The reference case for a 3-bet pot: the opener has a 4-bet opportunity, the 3-bettor
has a c-bet opportunity, and the flop is played with a low SPR.

Anna.role: hijack opener calling the 3-bet, then folding to the c-bet

Boris.role: cutoff 3-betting to 8bb and c-betting the flop

logic: Under the gun opens, the hijack calls, and the cutoff squeezes to 11bb; both
players in the pot fold.
A squeeze is also a 3-bet, which the pipeline records in both columns, and everyone
who had already put money in faces the squeeze.

Anna.role: hijack calling the open, then folding to the squeeze

Boris.role: cutoff squeezing over a raise and a caller

Frank.role: under the gun opener facing the squeeze

logic: Under the gun opens, the cutoff 3-bets, the opener 4-bets to 20bb and the cutoff
5-bets all-in for 100bb; the opener folds.
The reference case for a preflop all-in that is not called: the all-in player takes
the pot without showdown, and the chips returned uncalled must not be reported as
profit.

Boris.role: cutoff 3-betting, then 5-betting all-in and taking the pot

Frank.role: under the gun opening, 4-betting, then folding to the all-in

logic: The hijack opens, the cutoff calls, and the opener c-bets the flop of Ah 9d 4c;
the caller folds.
The smallest possible single-raised-pot c-bet: one opportunity, one fold to c-bet,
one pot of 6.5bb for the aggressor.

Boris.role: cutoff caller folding to the c-bet

logic: The hijack opens and the cutoff calls. Both check the flop, so the opener has no
c-bet; he bets the turn instead, which is a delayed c-bet, the caller calls, and
both check the river to showdown.
The only corpus hand where a delayed c-bet is followed by a showdown, so it also
covers showed-down, won-at-showdown and the river float opportunity.

Anna.role: hijack opener: no c-bet, delayed c-bet on the turn, then checks the river down

Boris.role: cutoff caller calling the turn, checking back the river, winning at showdown

logic: The hijack opens and the cutoff calls. The opener checks the flop and checks again
on the turn, so the caller gets to open the turn with no bet in front of him: that
bet is a probe, and it takes the pot down.
The probe is the counterpart of the delayed c-bet: same flop action, opposite actor.

Anna.role: hijack opener checking flop and turn, folding to the probe

Boris.role: cutoff caller probing the turn

logic: The cutoff opens and the button calls. The opener checks the flop, the caller bets
7bb into the aggressor (a donk bet), and the opener check-raises to 21bb and takes
the pot.
The reference case for a donk bet met by a check-raise: the response is recorded on
the player who faced the donk, and the raise size on the raiser.

Boris.role: cutoff opener checking and check-raising the donk bet

Cara.role: button caller donk betting the flop and folding to the check-raise

logic: The cutoff opens, the button calls, the opener c-bets the flop and the caller calls
in position. The opener then checks the turn and the caller bets: that bet is a
float, and the opener folds.
A float needs two things the golden corpus has to state explicitly: the caller must
be in position, and the floater bets only after the aggressor declines to barrel.

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting the flop, giving up the turn and folding

Cara.role: button caller floating the turn in position

logic: The cutoff opens, the button calls, and the opener c-bets the flop and barrels the
turn for 66 percent of the pot; the caller folds.
The turn barrel is faced by a player who called the flop c-bet in position, so the
same fold is recorded both as a fold to a turn c-bet and as the float situation.

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting the flop and barrelling the turn

Cara.role: button caller calling the flop c-bet and folding to the turn barrel

logic: The cutoff opens, the button calls, and the opener bets flop, turn and river with
the caller calling twice and folding on the river.
The only three-street barrel in the corpus, so it pins the per-street sizing of one
player across all three streets and the river fold response.

Boris.role: cutoff opener triple barrelling

Cara.role: button caller calling flop and turn, folding to the river barrel

logic: Under the gun opens, the hijack and the cutoff both call, so three players see the
flop. The opener bets 9bb into two players, the hijack calls and the cutoff folds;
the opener gives up the turn and folds to a bet.
The corpus reference for a multiway pot: three players on the flop, two on the turn,
and a caller who bets the turn after the aggressor checks is floating, not probing.

Anna.role: hijack caller calling the flop bet and betting the turn when checked to

Boris.role: cutoff caller folding to the flop bet

Frank.role: under the gun opener c-betting into two players, then folding the turn

logic: Under the gun opens, the hijack 3-bets to 8bb, the opener calls, and both players
get 92bb in on the flop of Ad Kd Qc: the opener shoves and the 3-bettor calls with
top set against a lower set, and the board runs out without a scare card.
Covers an all-in before the river with known hole cards, which is the case the
all-in EV and hand-strength work has to agree with.

Anna.role: hijack 3-betting, calling the flop shove with top set and winning

Frank.role: under the gun opening, calling the 3-bet, shoving the flop and losing

logic: Five identical single-raised pots that differ only in the flop, one per texture the
board classifier has to separate: ace-high rainbow, king-high two-tone, monotone,
paired and low connected. In each the opener c-bets 7bb into 13bb and takes it down.
Because the action is the same everywhere, any difference between these hands comes
from the board. The corpus asserts the stored flop cards; the texture flags #295 adds
are asserted by the subset of these hands that classifier gets wrong.

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting an ace-high rainbow flop

Cara.role: button caller folding to the c-bet

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting a king-high two-tone flop

Cara.role: button caller folding to the c-bet

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting a monotone flop

Cara.role: button caller folding to the c-bet

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting a paired flop

Cara.role: button caller folding to the c-bet

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting a low connected flop

Cara.role: button caller folding to the c-bet

logic: Ten identical single-raised pots in which the opener c-bets a different fraction of
the same 13bb pot, one per default sizing bucket from #296: 23, 31, 38, 46, 62, 77,
92, 123, 138 and 154 percent of the pot.
Every hand has the same actors, the same pot and the same board shape, so the only
variable is the size. The basis-point value the pipeline stores is pinned per hand;
the bucket each size falls into is named here for #296 to assert.

Boris.role: cutoff opener c-betting 3bb into 13bb (23 percent, bucket 0-25)
cutoff opener c-betting 4bb into 13bb (31 percent, bucket 25-33)
cutoff opener c-betting 5bb into 13bb (38 percent, bucket 33-40)
cutoff opener c-betting 6bb into 13bb (46 percent, bucket 40-50)
cutoff opener c-betting 8bb into 13bb (62 percent, bucket 50-66)
cutoff opener c-betting 10bb into 13bb (77 percent, bucket 66-80)
cutoff opener c-betting 12bb into 13bb (92 percent, bucket 80-100)
cutoff opener c-betting 16bb into 13bb (123 percent, bucket 100-125)
cutoff opener c-betting 18bb into 13bb (138 percent, bucket 125-150)
cutoff opener c-betting 20bb into 13bb (154 percent, bucket 150+)

logic: Under the gun open-limps, the cutoff over-limps and the big blind checks, so three
players see a flop nobody raised for. The limper bets the flop, the cutoff calls in
position and the big blind folds; the flop bettor gives up the turn and folds to the
cutoff's bet.
The corpus reference for a pot with no preflop aggressor: the flop bet belongs to no
continuation-bet chain at all, so it is the first bet of a limped pot, and the turn
bet that follows the flop bettor's check is a float like any other.

Frank.role: under the gun open-limping, betting the limped flop, then folding the turn

Boris.role: cutoff over-limping, calling the flop bet in position and betting the turn

Erin.role: big blind checking its option and folding the flop bet
